hints: Focus on what actually changes Kp and equilibrium position, and what only changes how fast you get there.

Write both equations out: $2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$ and $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$, then check the units of Kp for the Haber reaction.
Remember that a catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so think about what that means for yield and position.
walkthrough:
**Write the two equilibria**

Both reactions are reversible gas equilibria. Let's write them clearly.

$$2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$$
$$\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)$$

**Recall what controls Kp**

The value of $K_p$ changes only with temperature. Changing pressure, concentration or adding a catalyst does not change $K_p$ at constant T.

It may shift the position of equilibrium, but $K_p$ itself stays the same.

**Check catalysts**

A catalyst lowers activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions equally. It helps equilibrium to be reached faster, but it does not change $K_p$ or the position of equilibrium.

Also note the phases. In Haber, reactants are gases but the iron catalyst is a solid, so it is heterogeneous. In Contact, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is a solid with gaseous reactants, also heterogeneous.

options.A: Incorrect. For Haber, $K_p = p^2(\text{NH}_3) / [p(\text{N}_2) \times p^3(\text{H}_2)]$. That gives units of $\text{Pa}^{-2}$ (or $\text{atm}^{-2}$). Units cancel only when moles of gas are equal on both sides, which is not the case here (4 moles to 2 moles).
options.B: Incorrect. At constant temperature, $K_p$ is constant. Increasing pressure will shift the Contact equilibrium to the right (fewer moles of gas), increasing yield, but the value of $K_p$ does not fall.
options.C: Incorrect. The Haber process uses iron, a solid, with gaseous $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{H}_2$. Different physical states means a heterogeneous catalyst, not homogeneous.
options.D: Correct. $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is the catalyst for the Contact process. It speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but the position of equilibrium and $K_p$ are unchanged.
